scope: Initial targeted evidence map, not an exhaustive or systematic review. All MIRA primitives and drafts below require independent content, safety, applicability and rights review before publication.

sources.title: Improving early childhood development
sources.location: Publication overview; recommendations on responsive care and early learning
sources.access: Official overview inspected; full guideline appraisal pending
sources.summary: Recommends supporting responsive caregiving and early learning during the first three years, alongside wider family support.
sources.limit: Programme guidance is not validation of an individual MIRA activity, dose, material or age boundary.
sources.rights: Link and original summary only; no WHO text, illustrations or counselling cards reproduced.

sources.title: Care for Child Development
sources.access: Official overview inspected; manuals and cards require separate review
sources.summary: Combines play and communication with caregiver support to notice and respond to children's signals.
sources.limit: A trained service-delivery approach cannot be treated as evidence that a generated app activity achieves the same outcomes.
sources.rights: Link and original summary only; package adaptation rights not cleared.

sources.title: Parenting interventions to promote early child development in the first three years of life
sources.access: Abstract, methods/results sections and limitations inspected
sources.summary: Synthesizes 102 randomized trials across 33 countries; finds average benefits from parenting interventions across several child and parenting outcomes.
sources.limit: Substantial heterogeneity and variable reporting limit transfer to specific components. Programmes, not MIRA-generated micro-activities, were tested; only one intervention was virtual.
sources.rights: Link and original summary; no tables or study figures reused.

sources.title: 5 Steps for Brain-Building Serve and Return
sources.publisher: Harvard Center on the Developing Child
sources.summary: Explains responsive back-and-forth interaction between a child and an attentive adult.
sources.limit: An educational explanation is not a trial of this app or a prescription for a fixed number of exchanges.
sources.rights: Link and original summary only; no handout or five-step wording reproduced.

sources.title: Literacy Promotion: An Essential Component of Primary Care Pediatric Practice
sources.access: Publisher-indexed abstract inspected; full-page retrieval unavailable
sources.summary: Recommends encouraging shared reading from birth as part of relationship-supporting, language-rich family interactions.
sources.limit: Supports a broad practice, not compulsory book completion, early reading performance, or a specific book/material choice.
sources.rights: Link and original abstract summary only; full content and book rights not cleared.

sources.title: Nurturing care for early childhood development
sources.publisher: WHO / UNICEF / World Bank and partners
sources.access: Official overview inspected; full framework appraisal pending
sources.summary: Places early learning within a broader supportive environment, care, health, nutrition and safety context.
sources.limit: Does not justify maximizing scheduled activities, replacing care routines, or claims of guaranteed return for a family.
sources.rights: Link and original summary only; no framework graphics reused.

sources.title: Principles of Child Development and Learning and Implications That Inform Practice
sources.access: Official principles page inspected on 1 October 2026; underlying references not individually appraised
sources.summary: Frames play, child agency and interconnected domains across birth through age eight, with attention to individual, cultural and language context.
sources.limit: Professional guidance is not a trial of a MIRA activity or an age-specific material-safety approval. Do not infer an individual child's readiness.
sources.rights: Link and original summary only. No proprietary lesson text, images or supporting book content reproduced.

sources.title: Can guidance during play enhance children’s learning and development in educational contexts?
sources.location: Abstract; methods; risk of bias; discussion; limitations
sources.access: Publisher-indexed methods, results and limitations inspected on 1 October 2026; supplementary study-level extraction remains pending
sources.summary: Reviewed 39 studies; 17 entered meta-analysis. Some comparisons favoured guided play for mathematics, shape knowledge and task switching; other outcomes showed no detected difference.
sources.limit: High risk of bias, sparse outcome groups and heterogeneous delivery limit confidence. This does not establish a universally best method, home-app effectiveness or safety of generated activities.
sources.rights: Link and original summary only; no tables, figures or intervention scripts reproduced.

claims.text: Responsive caregiver-child interaction is a supported general direction for early-learning programmes.
claims.notSupported: A particular MIRA script, number of turns or developmental outcome.

claims.text: Play and everyday communication can be contexts for responsive caregiving.
claims.notSupported: Any invented material substitution or activity being safe for a particular child.

claims.text: Shared reading is recommended as a relationship-supporting language opportunity.
claims.notSupported: Accelerated reading, required sitting time or a validated effect from this draft.

claims.text: Learning opportunities belong within supportive care and family needs.
claims.notSupported: A scientifically established daily activity quota.

claims.text: Child choice and context-sensitive adult support are a professional-practice basis for play opportunities.
claims.scope: Professional practice guidance across birth through eight; not an activity prescription
claims.notSupported: A fixed age threshold, a required response, or approved hazards for a generated activity.

claims.text: Evidence for guided play varies by outcome and comparison; broad claims of superiority are not supported.
claims.notSupported: Guaranteed gains, prescribed doses or efficacy of a particular MIRA activity.

primitives.name: Respond to a child's signal
primitives.mechanism: An adult notices a voluntary sound or gesture, responds, and leaves room for another signal.
primitives.readiness: Individual comfort and communication context must be reviewed; no exact age prescription established.
constraints: Do not demand a response or count turns.
Do not touch or reposition the child as part of the generated draft.
Stop or pause when the child disengages.

primitives.name: Follow what catches their attention
primitives.mechanism: The adult attends to what the child is already noticing and offers a short, optional comment.
materials: Existing surroundings only; no new objects
primitives.readiness: Setting, access and supervision require review before a template can be published.
constraints: Do not introduce small parts, food, water, heights or new equipment.
Do not redirect attention to meet a task target.
A glance away or refusal is a valid ending.
contexts: Noticing through a window from an existing comfortable position

primitives.name: Share attention around a book
primitives.mechanism: An adult and child explore an available book together without needing to finish it.
materials: One existing book; suitability and condition still require review
primitives.readiness: Book format, positioning and material risks need age-specific content review.
constraints: Do not introduce book modifications or material substitutions.
No reading test, required words or page-completion target.
No copyrighted story excerpts; generate only original caregiver phrasing.

primitives.name: Make room for language in a routine
primitives.mechanism: The adult uses brief, responsive language around something already happening.
primitives.readiness: Select a routine where the adult can remain fully attentive to care and safety.
constraints: Do not add feeding, sleep, medical or physical-care instructions.
Do not distract the adult from essential care.
Use a comfortable caregiver language; no promised bilingual outcomes.
contexts: Getting ready to leave a room

primitives.name: Answer a voluntary expression
primitives.mechanism: The adult acknowledges or gently echoes a child-initiated sound or expression.
primitives.readiness: Sensory comfort and individual communication differences need review.
constraints: Do not prescribe mouth movements, motor exercises or physical manipulation.
Do not require eye contact, speech or imitation from the child.
No loud sounds, rewards, tests or repetitions quota.

primitives.name: Tell a small story about ordinary life
primitives.mechanism: An adult offers an original, brief account of a familiar event, leaving room for the child's response.
primitives.readiness: Language complexity and context require review; not a prescribed milestone task.
constraints: No invented family facts or cultural assumptions.
No frightening themes, factual teaching claims or copyrighted stories.
No question testing or required recall.
contexts: An ordinary sound in the room

primitives.name: Join a pretend idea without taking over
primitives.mechanism: The adult follows a pretend idea initiated by the child, leaving the child in control of the direction.
primitives.readiness: Requires a child-initiated pretend context; applicability and alternatives for different communication needs need review. Not an infant prescription.
constraints: Do not introduce props, costumes, food, physical positioning or new equipment.
Do not assign a role, demand speech or turn pretend play into a test.
The child may change the idea, decline company or stop.
contexts: The child invites an adult into a pretend idea
The child changes the direction of an existing pretend idea

primitives.name: Stay with a comparison they notice
primitives.mechanism: The adult acknowledges a comparison initiated by the child without asking for a correct answer.
materials: Existing surroundings only; no new objects
primitives.readiness: Child interest, setting and communication access require review. No exact age or sorting/counting expectation is established.
constraints: Do not collect, move or introduce materials, food, water or small parts.
No sorting test, counting quota, correct-answer prompt or performance praise.
Do not infer mathematical ability from a response; turning away ends the invitation.
contexts: A child notices a visible difference in the surroundings
A child points out something that seems similar
